title: Code Scan lifecycle — find the brand leak and the slow Lamp Week page
feature: Devin Code Scans: Security Swarm vs performance and accessibility scan types, scan profiles, the Findings tab, Assign to Devin, dismissal, Scan new commits and SARIF export
prerequisites: Lab 00 done (or you know the Harbourline brands and planted-defect rule)
Repo connected to your Devin org; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` done at the root
Your Devin role includes the Use code scans permission (see section 6)

matrix.integration: Devin Code Scans (Security page) — run, read and act on findings
matrix.fixture: Read the committed reference findings in labs/05-code-scans/fixtures/findings.json
matrix.note: Needs the org permission Use code scans; code scanning must be enabled for the org

matrix.integration: Devin Code Scans — create or edit shared scan profiles
matrix.fixture: Use an existing profile, or run Security with the defaults and type your focus as extra guidance
matrix.note: Needs Manage code scans; without it ask an admin to create the profiles you design

matrix.integration: GitHub write access for the Devin app (Assign to Devin opens a PR)
matrix.fixture: Skip the PR step and describe the fix branch you would expect; the facilitator shows a closed demo PR
matrix.note: The PR must target a throwaway branch or be closed unmerged — never merge a plant fix into main

matrix.integration: Local stack (Postgres, services/api) to confirm a finding
matrix.fixture: Un-skip the matching test in services/api/test/planted.test.ts on a throwaway branch
matrix.note: Optional: proves a finding is real before you assign it

credentials.fixture_only_story: Without scan permissions you work from the committed findings export (titles, severities, statuses, locations and triage notes); open each cited file to judge its reasoning yourself: classify every finding (real, duplicate, false positive), choose which one you would assign and which you would dismiss and with what note, then run the drill. You still answer every acceptance criterion in writing; criteria 5–8 are marked observer-only.
not_exercised: Creating scans and profiles without the Manage code scans permission
Opening the remediation PR without GitHub write access for the Devin app

scenarios.clean_state: `main` is at the latest commit with every planted defect intact (`services/api/PLANTED.md`, `apps/web/PLANTED.md`). Your org may already contain the facilitator's reference scans from 22 Oct 2026 — read them but start your own. No open lab-05 remediation PR is yours yet.

injectors.name: fixture-false-positive
injectors.behaviour: The fixtures and contract stub (`scenarios/`, `fixtures/mcp/`, `.env.example`) contain a fake PayGate secret. A scan may flag it as a hard-coded credential. Decide whether it is real, and if not dismiss it with a note a security reviewer would accept.

injectors.name: no-new-commits
injectors.behaviour: Press Scan new commits before anything has landed on main. Observe what happens and explain it to the customer in one sentence.

injectors.name: permission-downgrade
injectors.behaviour: The facilitator moves you to a role with Use but not Manage code scans. You can still run scans and assign findings, but the profile editor is read-only. Carry on without asking for the role back.

injectors.name: lamp-week-proof
injectors.behaviour: On a throwaway branch with the `n-plus-one` test un-skipped, the test reports the statement count for the Lamp Week collection — the number the CTO will ask for.
